content: I used a long tweezers and a needlenose pliers and didn't have too much trouble.  Insert the ziptie, use the tweezers to grab the far end and bend it out enough to get a good grip with the needlenose, and pull it through.

Didn't we have a tool for guiding these zip ties when we did this originally? It'd be good for the kit to include that, or at least to mention it as an optional printable part or for anyone that still has it from the original assembly.

Edit: Here it is, it's the "ASSEMBLY MULTI TOOL R2" from the Core One printable parts: https://www.printables.com/model/1167816-core-onegen-2-printable-parts/files

Here's the documentation on how to use this tool once printed, much easier than without it, and I didn't find the cables already being present to be much of an issue. https://help.prusa3d.com/guide/3-back-assembly_835506#839658

Its almost impossible to get the 3rd tie to go behind all the cables and appear in front of the motherboard. Your picture shows nowhere near the number of cables in that area. These ties should be added as the original kit suggested before all the cables where in the way.

Ended up using one of the allen keys to *carefully* hook the end of the tie and pull it in front of the circuitboard. Not an ideal situation with electronics right near,
